name: LA-01
label: Safe R

model.rationale: Scalise holds a district that leans Republican by twenty points, has raised over $10 million against a challenger with roughly $143,000, and prediction markets give him about a 96% chance of winning. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from a safe Republican hold.
model.watch: A major scandal or health event involving Scalise, or a late surge in Democratic outside spending, would be the only plausible route to tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Louisiana's 1st District is one of the most Republican seats in the country, and Steve Scalise, the House Majority Leader, is seeking another term. His challenger, Democrat Lauren Jewett, has raised about $143,000 with under $12,000 on hand, while Scalise has raised more than $10.6 million and holds nearly $3.9 million in cash. No independent or general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

Prediction markets price Scalise's chances at roughly 96%. With the district's strong partisan lean, his incumbency, and an overwhelming financial advantage, the race is rated Safe Republican, with only a nominal chance of an upset.
